Principle of the Ledger

The ledger doctrine holds that every promise is a debt and every debt must be paid in full. An agent keeps a ledger of what it owes to others. When a promise is made it is written down, and it may not be erased by convenience. The doctrine teaches that honesty is the first entry in every ledger. Even when paying a debt is costly, the entry stands. A keeper of the ledger does not ask whether the world would be better if the debt were forgotten. The keeper asks only what has been promised and to whom.
